Samantha —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our mutual action plan (MAP), I attached a first-draft evaluation plan and a short concurrency playbook that maps the performance gates we agreed on: 95th-pct latency <= 250ms for single-turn generation, TTFT <= 120ms for cached prefix, and sustained throughput targets for 1k qps steady-state with burst probes to 5k qps.

Attachments included: acme_map_v1.pdf (MAP + evaluation checklist), concurrency_results_q3.csv (blank template for results).

Key asks from Redwood for the validation window:
- Confirm the target API payload shape and sequence length distribution (suggested: 12 tokens prompt, 128 tokens generation).
- Approve scheduled test dates: May 26 (burst probes) and May 28â€”30 (steady-state ramp).
- Provide a point of contact for on-call during tests (we recommend someone who can toggle client-side rate limits quickly).

What we'll run on our side: an end-to-end MAP plan with three phases — baseline single-client latency, controlled burst probes, and multi-client steady-state with queueing instrumentation. We'll instrument TTFT (time-to-first-token), end-to-end p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, per-server queue length, and rejection rates.

Please review the attached MAP and confirm. If OK, we'll lock the dates and share pre-test knobs for your infra team.

Thanks,

Samantha —

Great questions; answers inline below and Iâ€™ve attached a brief engineering note: acme_map_v1.pdf (see section 3).

1) Burst profile: we recommend stepped bursts for the production-like behavior you described. Suggested schedule: 5m warmup @ 500 qps, then 3m@1k, 3m@3k, 5m@5k with a 10m cooldown. Stepped bursts let us observe queue build-up and recoverability.

2) TTFT measurement: we record TTFT at the edge (client-side) and server-first-byte at the model runtime. Cache-hit vs cache-miss is derived from our KV prefix cache logs (we tag requests where prefix cache returned a complete KV hit). For your evaluation we'll provide both client-observed TTFT and server-first-token timestamps so you can map cache delta.

3) Sample run: Marcus attached a trimmed CSV excerpt from a partner run that mirrors your profile (concurrency_results_q3.csv). It includes timestamps, qps buckets, p50/p90/p95, token/s, queue_length, and early-reject counts.

Next steps: if you sign off on stepped bursts and the dates, we'll schedule a 30-min pre-test sync May 25 to walk infra knobs (timeouts, client retry backoff, and token bucket rate caps).

Thanks,
Jonas

Subject: Re: MAP: Performance validation & concurrency playbook for AcmeAI — runbook & trimmed results

Team / Samantha —

Attaching a trimmed run summary we ran internally against a similar workload last week. Highlights:
- Test profile: 12-token prompt / 128-token completion, mixed sampling.
- Burst probes (stepped): 5m@500 warm, 3m@1k, 3m@3k, 5m@5k, 10m cooldown.
- Steady-state: sustained 1k qps for 60 minutes across 10 workers.

Key findings (see concurrency_results_q3.csv for raw):
- TTFT (client-observed) at steady-state 1k qps: p50=78ms, p90=112ms, p95=145ms.
- Burst peak 5k qps: median TTFT jumped to 420ms with p95 at ~980ms during the 5k window; queue lengths on the router spiked to 42 requests per GPU prior to shedding.
- Early rejects: 2.1% at peak due to proactive rate-limiter kicks (we configured a soft limit at 80% of pool capacity).
- Tail latency drivers: queue saturation + token-gen slowdowns on long sequences; we did not see model OOMs but observed increased kernel-level scheduling variance.

Recommendations for controlled test with AcmeAI:
1) Enable stepped bursts (as above) but cap client-side concurrency to limit queue spikes: recommend per-client socket limit of 256 concurrent inflight requests.
2) Tune soft-rate limits: set soft_limit = 0.7 * pool_capacity, hard_limit = pool_capacity. Soft limit will cause early backpressure signals instead of bulk rejects.
3) Shorten retry backoff for burst probes (linear retry 200ms x 3) to avoid synchronized retries that worsen queues.
4) Observe TTFT split: capture edge vs runtime first-token timestamps; reuse Redwood helper script (we'll provide) to compute cache-hit delta.

I'll attach the CSV excerpt as concurrency_results_q3.csv (12KB trimmed).

- Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
